senses.gloss: The wooden or metal frame that holds the glass in a window and slides up and down.
examples: The bottom *sash* sticks unless you push both sides at once.
Painters had sealed the *sash* shut with three coats of latex.
We replaced the rotted *sashes* on the front of the house.

senses.gloss: Alcohol, in informal talk about someone who drinks too much.
examples: He's been off the *sauce* since January.
After the divorce he hit the *sauce* pretty hard.
Her uncle finally gave up the *sauce* for good.

senses.gloss: An old saying that everyone has heard many times.
examples: He trotted out the old *saw* about money not buying happiness.
The book opens with the familiar *saw* that history repeats itself.
Grandpa had a *saw* ready for every occasion.

senses.gloss: A worker who stays on the job during a strike, or one hired to replace a striker.
examples: The union called anyone who crossed the picket line a *scab*.
The plant kept running with *scabs* bused in from out of state.
Nobody in that family would ever work as a *scab*.

senses.gloss: The size or extent of something, especially when it is very large.
examples: Nobody expected a disaster on this *scale*.
The company farms on a *scale* no family operation can match.
The photos give you some idea of the *scale* of the damage.

senses.gloss: A range of numbers or levels used for measuring or ranking something.
examples: Rate your pain on a *scale* of one to ten.
The quake measured 6.1 on the Richter *scale*.
Salaries follow a fixed *scale* based on years of service.

senses.gloss: The ratio between a distance on a map or model and the real distance.
examples: At this *scale*, one inch equals a mile.
The whole model is built to *scale*.
Check the *scale* in the corner before you measure the trail.

senses.gloss: One of the small thin plates that cover the body of a fish or reptile.
examples: He scraped the *scales* off the trout with the back of a knife.
The snake's *scales* caught the light as it moved.
A single silver *scale* was stuck to the cutting board.

senses.gloss: A series of musical notes going up or down in fixed steps.
examples: She practices *scales* for twenty minutes every morning.
Beginners start with the C major *scale*.
He can play every *scale* without looking at his hands.

senses.gloss: A quick look through something to find or check the main points.
examples: A quick *scan* of the menu told me there was nothing for vegetarians.
Give the contract a *scan* before the meeting.
One *scan* of the room and she knew he wasn't there.

senses.gloss: A digital copy of a document or photo made by a scanner.
examples: Email me a *scan* of your driver's license.
The *scan* came out crooked, so I did it again.
They keep *scans* of every receipt in a shared folder.

senses.gloss: A radio receiver that picks up police, fire, and other emergency broadcasts.
examples: He keeps a *scanner* going in the kitchen all night.
Reporters heard about the fire on the police *scanner*.
The *scanner* crackled with calls all through the storm.

senses.gloss: Lasting emotional damage left by a painful experience.
examples: The war left *scars* that never really healed.
You can hear the *scars* of that childhood when she talks about her family.
Losing the farm left a *scar* on all of them.

senses.gloss: The place where something happened, especially a crime or an accident.
examples: Police were on the *scene* within four minutes.
He left the *scene* of the accident without stopping.
Reporters were kept a block away from the *scene*.

senses.gloss: A noisy public display of anger or emotion.
examples: Please don't make a *scene* in front of the neighbors.
She caused quite a *scene* at the restaurant.
He walked out rather than have a *scene* in the lobby.

senses.gloss: A particular area of activity together with the people involved in it.
examples: Austin has a great live music *scene*.
She's been part of the art *scene* here for years.
The city's restaurant *scene* has changed completely.

senses.gloss: The painted backgrounds and structures used on a theater stage.
examples: Volunteers spent the weekend painting *scenery*.
The *scenery* for the second act rolls on from the wings.
They store the old *scenery* in a warehouse behind the theater.

senses.gloss: A pleasant smell.
examples: The *scent* of fresh bread filled the kitchen.
I love the *scent* of lilacs in May.
A faint *scent* of coffee drifted down the hall.

senses.gloss: An arrangement of parts that are chosen to go together, especially colors in a design.
examples: The whole apartment follows a gray and white color *scheme*.
We picked a *scheme* of soft blues for the nursery.
The poem keeps the same rhyme *scheme* all the way through.

senses.gloss: A deep spoon or small shovel for lifting loose food.
examples: Use the *scoop* in the flour bin, not a coffee cup.
The ice cream *scoop* is in the top drawer.
He dug into the dog food with a plastic *scoop*.

senses.gloss: The amount that such a spoon holds.
examples: I'll take two *scoops* of chocolate in a cone.
Add one *scoop* of protein powder to the milk.
She ordered a single *scoop* and ate it in the car.

senses.gloss: The range of subjects or activity that something deals with.
examples: That question is outside the *scope* of this report.
The investigation widened in *scope* over the summer.
We had to narrow the *scope* of the project to finish on time.

senses.gloss: Someone whose job is to look for talented players or performers.
examples: *Scouts* from three colleges came to watch him pitch.
A *scout* saw her play in a summer league.
The team's *scouts* spend the whole season on the road.

senses.gloss: A boy or girl who belongs to a youth group that teaches camping and outdoor skills.
examples: The *scouts* sold popcorn outside the grocery store.
My son has been a *scout* since third grade.
A troop of *scouts* camped down by the river.

senses.gloss: The harsh sound made when something hard rubs against a surface.
examples: We heard the *scrape* of a shovel on the sidewalk.
The *scrape* of chairs filled the room as everyone stood up.
There was a *scrape*, and then the gate swung open.

senses.gloss: An awkward situation that someone gets into through carelessness.
examples: He got into a few *scrapes* as a teenager.
Her brother is always in some kind of *scrape*.
It took a good lawyer to get him out of that *scrape*.

senses.gloss: The starting point, with nothing prepared in advance, used mainly in the phrase from scratch.
examples: She makes the pie crust from *scratch*.
After the fire they had to start again from *scratch*.
The new coach built the program from *scratch*.

senses.gloss: The flat surface of a TV, computer, or phone on which images appear.
examples: My phone *screen* cracked when I dropped it.
He stares at a *screen* all day at work.
Her name came up on the *screen* right away.

senses.gloss: A movable panel used to divide a room or hide something from view.
examples: A folding *screen* separates the bed from the desk.
The nurse pulled a *screen* around the bed.
An old painted *screen* stood in the corner of the shop.

senses.gloss: A cruel or worthless person, or such people taken as a group.
examples: Anyone who steals from a food bank is *scum*.
The officers called them *scum* right to their faces.
He treated her like *scum* for years.

senses.gloss: A very large quantity of something spread out in front of you.
examples: He looked out from the stage at a *sea* of faces.
The parking lot was a *sea* of red taillights.
We waded through a *sea* of paperwork to get the permit.

senses.gloss: An official mark stamped on a document, or the stamp used to make it.
examples: The certificate carries the university's *seal*.
He broke the wax *seal* on the envelope.
Every page had to be stamped with the notary's *seal*.

senses.gloss: A ring or strip that closes a joint tightly so that nothing leaks through.
examples: The *seal* on the refrigerator door is cracked.
A bad *seal* let water into the trunk.
Don't buy it if the *seal* on the jar is broken.

senses.gloss: A layer of coal or ore lying between layers of rock.
examples: The mine follows a *seam* of coal three feet thick.
They struck a rich *seam* of silver in 1889.
The *seam* runs for miles under the mountain.

senses.gloss: An examination of a person, a bag, or a building by officers looking for something.
examples: The *search* of the apartment turned up nothing.
Officers need a warrant for a *search* like that.
A quick *search* at the gate found the knife.

senses.gloss: The part of the year when a particular sport, crop, or business is at its height.
examples: The football *season* starts in September.
Hotels double their rates during the busy *season*.
He hit thirty home runs last *season*.

senses.gloss: A set of episodes of a television show released over one period.
examples: The third *season* comes out in October.
We watched a whole *season* in one weekend.
The show was canceled after two *seasons*.

senses.gloss: A place on an elected body or a board, held by one member.
examples: She won a *seat* in the state senate.
The party lost twelve *seats* in the last election.
He holds a *seat* on the school board.

senses.gloss: The place where a government, court, or organization is based.
examples: Washington is the *seat* of the federal government.
The county *seat* is thirty miles north of here.
For centuries the town was the *seat* of the local bishop.

senses.gloss: The method or quality that explains why something works so well.
examples: The *secret* to a good crust is very cold butter.
Everyone wants to know the *secret* of her energy.
He says the *secret* is starting early and never rushing.

senses.gloss: One of the parts that a place, an object, or a group is divided into.
examples: We sat in the family *section* behind home plate.
The middle *section* of the bridge was floated into place.
The brass *section* stood up for the last chorus.

senses.gloss: A player or team ranked in advance in a tournament.
examples: She's the top *seed* going into the tournament.
The number one *seed* lost in the first round.
Two of the top four *seeds* were knocked out on Tuesday.

senses.gloss: The small beginning of something that later grows much bigger.
examples: That trip planted the *seed* of the whole business.
The report sowed *seeds* of doubt about the company.
His remark planted a *seed* she couldn't ignore.

senses.gloss: The act of taking something away by force or by legal authority.
examples: The *seizure* of the shipment made the evening news.
Agents reported the largest drug *seizure* of the year.
The law allows the *seizure* of property used in a crime.

senses.gloss: A product that sells well.
examples: That jacket is our best *seller*.
The plain black mug turned out to be a big *seller*.
Cookbooks are steady *sellers* around the holidays.

senses.gloss: Someone who gives up their principles for money or success.
examples: Fans called the band *sellouts* after the commercial.
He'd rather stay poor than be a *sellout*.
There's a fine line between growing up and being a *sellout*.

senses.gloss: A meeting at which a subject is taught or discussed, held for professionals or the public.
examples: The bank runs a free *seminar* on buying your first home.
She flew to Dallas for a two-day sales *seminar*.
The *seminar* covers everything from taxes to insurance.

senses.gloss: An older person, especially one who has retired.
examples: The theater offers a discount for *seniors*.
The center serves lunch to about eighty *seniors* a day.
Many *seniors* in the county live alone.

senses.gloss: A feeling or awareness of something.
examples: I felt a huge *sense* of relief when the call finally came.
He has no *sense* of direction at all.
There's a growing *sense* that nothing will change.

senses.gloss: One of the meanings of a word or phrase.
examples: The word has at least four *senses* in this dictionary.
In what *sense* are you using the word free?
He meant it in the older *sense* of the word.

senses.gloss: A long, tiresome lecture about how someone ought to behave.
examples: I got a *sermon* about my grades all the way home.
I don't need a *sermon* about being ten minutes late.
Every dinner ended with one of his *sermons* about money.

senses.gloss: Someone who brings food and drinks to customers in a restaurant.
examples: Our *server* took the whole order without writing anything down.
The restaurant is hiring *servers* for the summer.
Tip your *server* at least twenty percent.

senses.gloss: A flat utensil for lifting a slice of food onto a plate.
examples: Cut the pie and use the *server* to lift out the first slice.
The set came with a cake knife and a *server*.
She washed the silver *server* by hand.

senses.gloss: A religious ceremony held in a church or at a funeral.
examples: The *service* starts at ten on Sunday.
A memorial *service* is planned for Saturday morning.
We got to the church halfway through the *service*.

senses.gloss: A system that supplies something the public needs, such as transport or mail.
examples: Bus *service* to the airport runs every twenty minutes.
Ice knocked out power and phone *service* for two days.
The town has no rail *service* anymore.

senses.gloss: The armed forces, or a period spent in them.
examples: He joined the *service* right out of high school.
Both of her sons are in the *service*.
He was wounded during his second year of *service*.

senses.gloss: A group of things that belong together and are used together.
examples: I lost my whole *set* of keys.
They gave us a *set* of steak knives as a wedding gift.
A chess *set* was laid out on the table by the window.

senses.gloss: One of the parts that a tennis or volleyball match is divided into.
examples: She won the first *set* six to four.
The match went to five *sets*.
He dropped the second *set* but came back strong.

senses.gloss: A block of songs that a band or DJ plays without a break.
examples: The band played a short *set* and left.
They open every *set* with the same three songs.
Her second *set* ran past midnight.

senses.gloss: The place and surroundings in which something happens or stands.
examples: The inn sits in a beautiful *setting* above the lake.
It was an odd *setting* for a business meeting.
The garden makes a lovely *setting* for a wedding.

senses.gloss: The time and place in which a story or film takes place.
examples: The novel's *setting* is a small town in the 1930s.
The *setting* shifts to Chicago in the second half.
Half the class missed the question about the *setting*.

senses.gloss: A trick arranged to fool someone or to make an innocent person look guilty.
examples: He swore the whole thing was a *setup*.
It looked like a robbery, but it was a *setup*.
The meeting turned out to be a *setup* from the start.

senses.gloss: A cover pulled down over a window, or the cover over a lamp.
examples: Pull the *shades* down before the sun hits that window.
She raised the *shade* and looked out at the street.
The lamp in the hall needs a new *shade*.

senses.gloss: A particular variety or depth of a color.
examples: The wall is a darker *shade* of blue than I wanted.
They sell the same shirt in eight *shades* of gray.
Her hair had gone a lighter *shade* over the summer.

senses.gloss: A slight difference or a small amount of something.
examples: The two words carry different *shades* of meaning.
There was a *shade* of doubt in his voice.
Every answer came with a *shade* of sarcasm.

senses.gloss: A vertical passage in a building for an elevator or for air.
examples: The elevator *shaft* runs the full height of the building.
A pigeon got into the air *shaft* and couldn't get out.
They found her keys at the bottom of the *shaft*.

senses.gloss: The long straight handle or rod of a tool, a club, or an arrow.
examples: The *shaft* of the golf club is graphite.
He gripped the *shaft* of the axe close to the head.
The arrow's *shaft* snapped on impact.

senses.gloss: A narrow beam of light.
examples: A *shaft* of sunlight came through the barn door.
*Shafts* of light cut through the dust in the attic.
One *shaft* of light fell across the kitchen floor.

senses.gloss: The condition that a person or thing is in.
examples: He's in good *shape* for a man of seventy.
The car is in rough *shape* but it still runs.
The roof is in better *shape* than we expected.

senses.gloss: The part of something that belongs to one person or that one person does.
examples: You haven't done your *share* of the dishes.
Each of the kids got an equal *share* of the money.
She's had more than her *share* of bad luck.

senses.gloss: A person who cheats others or lends money at cruel rates.
examples: He borrowed from a loan *shark* and never got clear of it.
Watch out for *sharks* at that end of the business.
The quiet old man turned out to be a pool *shark*.

senses.gloss: A narrow escape from danger or trouble, used in the phrase a close shave.
examples: That was a close *shave*; the truck missed us by inches.
He's had a couple of close *shaves* on that highway.
We passed the inspection, but it was a close *shave*.

senses.gloss: The hard outer covering of an egg or a nut.
examples: Pick the bits of *shell* out of the bowl.
The egg *shells* go in the compost.
Crack the walnut and throw the *shell* away.

senses.gloss: A large explosive projectile fired from a big gun.
examples: *Shells* landed on the far side of the river all night.
A *shell* took out the top floor of the building.
The museum has an unexploded *shell* from the war.

senses.gloss: The outer walls of a building left standing after fire or ruin.
examples: Only the brick *shell* of the factory is left.
The fire left a blackened *shell* where the store had been.
They built a new house inside the old *shell*.

senses.gloss: Anything that protects a person or thing from harm.
examples: Sunscreen is your best *shield* against burns.
The heat *shield* on the spacecraft held.
Her lawyer acted as a *shield* between her and the press.

senses.gloss: A change in position, opinion, or the way things are done.
examples: There's been a real *shift* in public opinion since spring.
The company made a *shift* toward online sales.
A small *shift* in the wind saved the town.

senses.gloss: The key on a keyboard that makes capital letters.
examples: Hold *shift* and press the letter.
The *shift* key on this laptop sticks.
Caps lock is right above *shift* on the left.
